Enumerations.EnumerationDescription: The basic data type of a scalar field

EnumeratedValues.EnumeratedValueDescription: The scalar field holds binary values
The scalar field holds true/false values
The scalar field holds integer values
The scalar field holds values that represent a date, datetime or time
The scalar field holds numeric values
The scalar field holds string values
The scalar field holds XML values

Enumerations.EnumerationDescription: The type of relationship that exists between two concepts

EnumeratedValues.EnumeratedValueDescription: The parent concept forms part of the unique identifier for the child concept, and acts as the unique container when the model is expressed in a hierarchical structure
The parent concept forms part of the unique identifier for the child concept, but does not act as the unique container
The parent concept provides non-identifying, descriptive detail about the child concept

Enumerations.EnumerationDescription: The type of concept, either Data Type, Enumeration, Object, Scalar, UniqueKey or SubType

EnumeratedValues.EnumeratedValueDescription: The concept represents a Data Type
The concept represents an Enumeration
The concept represents an Entity (i.e. a class of object)
The concept represents a scalar-valued property (either a Domain or a Field)
The concept represents a particular unique key through which an Entity may be referenced
The concept represents an Entity Subtype (i.e. a particular specialised variant of a class of object)

Enumerations.EnumerationDescription: The detailed manner in which the relationship is expressed within hierarchical structures such as XML documents or JSON documents

EnumeratedValues.EnumeratedValueDescription: The primary entity contains a reference to the secondary entity
Multiple instances of the secondary entity are nested within the primary entity
Nesting is used to fully describe the single instance of the secondary entity which is referenced by the primary entity

Nesting is used to partially describe the single instance of the secondary entity which is referenced by the primary entity.  The nested item is a "reference" which holds more than just an identifier - it also contains some additional information about the referenced object, with the aim of reducing the need for the secondary entity to be fetched separately.
The secondary entity extends the primary entity, providing additional information that is relevant to a particular of that entity.
A single instance of the secondary entity is nested within the primary entity
The relationship forms part of the path between two entities, but it is not exposed within hierarchical renderings: it is "collapsed" or "passed-through") .

Enumerations.EnumerationDescription: The type of control that should be used when collecting data for this field

EnumeratedValues.EnumeratedValueDescription: A dropdown list should be rendered
A searchable text box should be rendered

A model, made primarily of scalar concepts and object concepts
A family of properties
A field or relationship

A unique key index that can be used to uniquely identify objects of a particular type
A record that associates a given unique key with a particular family of properties, signifying that the family of properties is relevant to that unique key
A data type
A constrained vocabulary
An item within a constrained vocabulary
A Linq expression, starting from the current entity, that defines an item to be hydrated when hydrating the current entity
A prefix that can be placed before the name of the current entity to specify the role it plays
A variant of a Concept with primary key PK2_CommonConcept
A variant of a Concept with primary key PK3_ScalarConcept
A variant of a Concept with primary key PK4_ObjectConcept
A variant of a Concept with primary key PK5_UniqueKeyConcept
A variant of a Concept with primary key PK6_SubTypeConcept
A Common variant of a Concept
